record.question: Which of the following activities is not allowed for a government servant?
options: Participating in an amateur sports activity
Occasionally publishing a book novel
Occasionally investing in the stock market through a licensed stock broker
Participate in the making of a privately produced media programme
record.explanation: Under the Conduct Rules, 1964, participating in the making of a privately produced media programme is restricted without sanction, while the other options (sports, occasional book publishing, occasional investment through a licensed broker) are not barred in the same way. The stem's wording of 'not allowed' points to option (d).

record.question: A day cannot be marked as dies-non:
options: when an official remains absent from duty without prior information
when on duty in office, the official leaves the office without proper permission
when the official arrives late for work
when the official remains in office, but refuses to perform duty assigned to him
record.explanation: Dies-non applies to a day of absence from duty, so a day cannot be marked dies-non merely because the official arrived late, which is a lapse of time rather than absence. The other options describe absence or non-performance of duty while present.

record.question: Which of the following amounts to a penalty as per CCS(CCA) Rules, 1965?
options: Compulsory retirement of a government servant in accordance with the provisions relating to his superannuation or retirement
recovery from his pay of the whole or part of a pecuniary loss caused by him
reversion of a government servant appointment on probation to any other service, grade or post to a lower service unconnected to his conduct
non-promotion of a government servant, whether in substantive or officiating capacity, after consideration of his case, to a service grade or post for promotion to which he is eligible
record.explanation: Recovery from pay of the whole or part of a pecuniary loss caused by the government servant is a minor penalty under Rule 11 of CCS(CCA) Rules, 1965. Compulsory retirement on superannuation, reversion of a probationer unconnected with conduct, and non-promotion are not penalties under that rule.
